text: A disgraced safecracker is released from prison with nothing but a bus ticket and a debt to the man who put him there. To clear it he must assemble a crew for one last job: the vault of a private bank in Marseille that holds the ledgers of half the city's politicians. The crew is a mess of old grudges, the plan has a hole in it that everyone can see, and the police inspector who caught him the first time has been waiting six years for him to try again. When the job goes wrong on the night, he has to choose between the money, his crew and the daughter who thinks he went straight.

A retired schoolteacher moves back to the seaside village where she grew up, intending to garden and nothing else. In the first week the organist of the parish church is found dead in the bell tower, and the local sergeant, who was her worst pupil, asks for her help because she is the only person in the village everyone will talk to. Each episode brings a new puzzle: a stolen regatta trophy, a poisoned prize marrow, a widow who is not quite a widow. Gentle, funny and very English, with a slow-burning friendship at its heart and a village full of secrets that are rarely as dark as they first appear.

The summer he turns sixteen, Teodor is sent to his grandmother's farm in the hills after his parents' marriage falls apart. He expects boredom. Instead he finds a neighbour his own age, Luca, who teaches him to repair motorbikes and to lie to the priest, and a feeling he has no words for yet. The novel follows one summer of heat, silence and small rebellions, as Teodor learns what his family will and will not forgive. A quiet, aching book about first love, shame and the courage it takes to be seen.

You wake up in the flooded maintenance deck of a research station eleven kilometres under the Pacific with no memory of the last thirty days. The crew is gone. Something moves in the dark water between the modules. Survive with scarce oxygen and a flickering torch, scavenge parts to repair the station's systems, and piece together the logs that explain what the crew found in the trench and why they opened the hatch. Inventory is limited, enemies cannot be killed, only avoided, and every sound you make is heard. A slow, oppressive descent into the deep, with a story that rewards those who read every note.

In 1987 a 19-year-old bank clerk left her shift in a small town in Saskatchewan and was never seen again. Her car was found running at a railway crossing. The police closed the case in 1991. Over twelve episodes, two journalists reopen it: they track down the officers, the boyfriend who was cleared, the manager who was never questioned, and a witness who changed her story three times. With new interviews, the original case files and a forensic review of the evidence, the series asks who knew what, and why nobody asked.

Pip, a small and very anxious hedgehog, has never left the hedge. When the Great Oak that shelters her village is sold to be cut down, she sets out with a boastful magpie and a sleepy toad to find the legendary Gardener who, the stories say, can talk to people. Their journey across one enormous back garden takes them past a lawnmower, a pond full of opinions and a cat who is not as scary as he looks. A warm, funny tale about courage in small packages, with songs.

Winter 1942. A battalion of conscripts is ordered to hold a ruined grain silo on the bank of a frozen river for ten days while the army regroups behind them. Told through the eyes of a young lieutenant who has never fired at a man and the veteran sergeant who despises him, the film follows the ten days hour by hour: the shelling, the hunger, the executions of deserters, the boy who dies in the snow asking for his mother. Unflinching about the brutality of the siege and the cynicism of the commanders who ordered it, and about the strange loyalty that grows between men who expect to die.

A workaholic logistics manager is sent to a snowbound alpine village to shut down an unprofitable toy warehouse three weeks before Christmas. The warehouse is run by a cheerful widower with two children, a dog and a complete inability to read a spreadsheet. She gives him until the 24th to turn it around. Between a lost shipment of nutcrackers, a village council that meets in the pub and a snowstorm that strands them together, the deadline starts to matter less than she expected. Light, cosy and sweetly predictable.

In the walled city of Vell, every citizen's memories are backed up nightly to the Archive, and anyone who commits a crime is simply restored to the person they were the day before it. Seventeen-year-old Ines works as an Archive technician until she discovers that her own memories have been rewritten four times. With a boy from the lower districts who has never been backed up at all, she goes looking for the version of herself that the city erased. The first book of a trilogy about memory, consent and who gets to decide what a person is.

A married architect begins an affair with a woman he meets at a gallery opening. She is beautiful, unattached and asks no questions, and for a month the affair is exactly what he wanted. Then she asks him for a key to his office, and the next week a client of his is found dead. The film follows his attempts to end the affair as it becomes clear she knows far more about his work, his wife and his finances than she should. Explicit, sweaty and increasingly paranoid, in the tradition of the nineties thriller.

Four episodes follow a year in the life of a single river, from the glacier where it begins to the delta where it meets the sea. Filmed over three years with underwater cameras and drones, the series shows the salmon run from the fish's point of view, a family of otters learning to hunt, the flood that reshapes the valley in a night, and the farmers, anglers and engineers whose lives depend on the water. Narrated calmly, with a quiet argument about what the river will look like in fifty years.

Three adult siblings return to their mother's noodle restaurant in Busan when she announces she is selling it. The eldest, a surgeon in Seoul, wants the money; the middle one, who never left, wants the restaurant; the youngest, a failed musician, wants their mother to say she is proud of him, just once. Over the seven days before the sale, old resentments surface at the dinner table, a buyer turns out to be a developer with plans for the whole street, and the mother reveals why she is really selling. Bittersweet and observant, with long dinner scenes and a great deal unsaid.
